title: Fault Mosaic: multi-dimensional failure taxonomy, tracehook routing, and dashboard spine
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a single, queryable dashboard + tracehook routing model that lets SREs and oncall engineers pivot across five fault axes (transport status codes, client-side timeouts/latency, service-side overload/backpressure, model-origin errors, and infra resource failures) and to route traces/metrics/logs to appropriate enrichment pipelines. This ticket covers taxonomy definition, tracehook enrichment rules, sampling policy, dashboard 'spine' implementation in Grafana, and SLO-linked alert contexts.

Motivation: Current error dashboards surface lots of signal but make it hard to answer compound questions such as: 'What fraction of 5xx spikes correlate with model tokenization errors vs upstream timeouts?' or 'Which models produce the highest rate of incomplete stream terminations under tail-latency?' The Fault Mosaic unifies axes and provides actionable routing so that high-value traces are forwarded to the model evaluation pipeline and infra traces are kept in the infra observability cluster.

Scope: 
- Finalize failure taxonomy and canonical labels used across logs/metrics/traces.
- Implement tracehook routing rules in the trace ingestion layer: label enrichment, adaptive sampling, and forward-to-queue rules.
- Produce a Grafana 'spine' dashboard that supports multi-axis pivoting, focused drilldowns, and prebuilt queries for common postmortem workflows.
- Wire alert contexts so pager alerts include top-3 likely causes from the Taxonomy and one-click links to correlated traces and model eval artifacts.
- Provide migration guide and mapping layer for legacy dashboards and alerts.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term ML-driven failure classifier (separate RFC), major infra migration to new observability cluster (coordination ticket exists).
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy doc published in Confluence with unique canonical labels for transport, runtime, model, infra, and client errors

Tracehook rules merged and deployed to staging that: (1) add taxonomy labels to incoming spans, (2) apply adaptive sampling to high-cardinality paths, (3) forward enriched spans to model-eval queue when model-error label present
Grafana spine dashboard deployed to staging with at least 5 pivot widgets: status-code breakdown, tail-latency slices, model-error heatmap, overload-correlated callgraph, and alert-context panel
Pager alerts in staging include taxonomy top-3 causes and direct links to correlated traces and the relevant model evaluation run when applicable
Migration mapping document completed with recommended mappings for 90% of existing dashboard panels and alert rules
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created. Draft taxonomy attached to Confluence link. Requested early input from runtime and model-onboarding teams.

2026-03-11 - Ravi Singh: Spike completed on tracehook router prototype. Found that adding taxonomy labels at the span root reduces cardinality explosion compared to per-event labels. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/4567
2026-03-12 - Mei Chen (SRE): Reviewed taxonomy draft; suggested splitting 'timeout' axis into 'client-timeout' and 'server-token-limit' to separate upstream vs model truncation cases.
2026-03-13 - Product review: PM requested the dashboard expose a one-click 'escalate to model team' button that attaches relevant model-id and token window to the incident. Added as AC item.

2026-03-14 - Ravi Singh: Started implementing adaptive sampling rule; measured reduction of high-cardinality spans from 320k/day to ~18k/day in local staging. Still iterating on sample bias to preserve rare model error cases.
notes: Design trade-offs: attaching labels at span root reduces indexing cost but requires careful propagation to child spans during batching. We will use a lightweight label set (<=6 labels) to avoid storage blowup.
Routing policy: prefer in-region forwarding; if model-error detected and model-owner team is external, forward an enriched copy to model-eval queue with PII redaction step.
Sampling policy: keep deterministic sampling for high-cardinality user IDs; use reservoir sampling for rare model error signals to retain examples for ML-driven classifier later.
Follow-ups: RFC for ML classifier (ENG-901201), infra migration coordination (ENG-901300), and SLO amendment proposal for model-side tail latency (PM-412).
